title: Survey on AI Ethics: A Socio-technical Perspective
measurement_description: The paper is a comprehensive survey on AI ethics and does not conduct original empirical measurements. It discusses religion primarily as an example of a sensitive or protected demographic attribute when defining algorithmic fairness, evaluating representation bias, and assessing stereotyping in foundation models.
findings: As a literature review, the paper notes that foundation models can capture and amplify social biases, including religious stereotyping, during pretraining or fine-tuning. It highlights that providing language models with under-informative contexts often reinforces existing social biases by generating stereotyped content, and cites existing studies that show persistent anti-Muslim bias in LLMs.
